description: Jan Evertsenstraat 151-153 odd and 158-160 even (late 1930s infill in the white-attic rows): brown brick, three storeys of one wide three-light window and one narrow two-light window per storey, a wide window and a pair of arched house doors on the ground, a tiled roof from 12.5 m with one broad dormer of three lights; some houses stack balconies with French doors on the narrow axis

dormer.note: one broad dormer of three lights in the tiled roof (151: 1.9-4.9 m, 13.3-15.3 m)

dormer-end.note: the dormer pushed to the end over the wide window (160, mirrored: 0.15-2.95 m of 5.28 m)

door-right.note: 151, 153: a wide window and the arched pair of house doors at the right

rhythm.bays: 2 axes: one wide three-light window, one narrow two-light window (or a French door on a balcony)
rhythm.groundFloor: residential: a wide window and an arched pair of doors
rhythm.roofline: tiled roof from a simple cornice at 12.5 m, one broad dormer
schemaLimits: the arched door heads are drawn square
the dormer's three lights are drawn as two lights in the kit's flat dormer

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2024-12-06 (ruler crop 32 px/m) of 151: wide windows 0.5-3.5 m and narrow 4.2-5.3 m at 3.9-5.8 / 6.9-8.75 / 9.85-11.7 m, the arched door pair 4.2-5.5 m on the ground, eaves 12.5 m, dormer 1.9-4.9 m at 13.3-15.3 m
strip.jpg 2024-12-06 of 153: the same body with a balcony stack (French doors) on the narrow axis
strip.jpg 2024-12-06 of 160 and 158: the same body, mirrored (narrow axis at the left), the dormer over the wide window on 160; 158 behind a tree

notes: Placed on evertsen-145-155 and evertsen-152-160 (lane de-baarsjes-faces-20261016). mirror: true puts the narrow axis (and the doors) at the left.
